purpose: Fixed report fields for independent simulated participant 2; observations are limited to the visible application.
persona: Independent simulated beginner, first introduction to RILL, interested in a small electronic dance groove.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The empty-lane hint led directly to MIDI and instrument assignment. Notes, group copies, naming, saving, and both exports were achievable with the mouse. Duplicate and precise trimming required extra discovery.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark arrangement, teal waveforms, visible note thumbnails, and restrained transport looked cohesive and readable. The very large empty lower area and dense tool row felt utilitarian.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most note edits and copies responded promptly. Native save dialogs sometimes appeared only after another screenshot, and WAV export had a noticeable wait with a useful elapsed-time indicator. No hardware-performance inference is intended.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Low overall confusion after the initial hints. I first dragged with Duplicate and got no copy; Tool help clarified that clicking was required. Fine trimming at the zoomed-out scale also took a snap change.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The visible app supported audio arrangement, a native VST3 instrument, piano-roll editing, mouse-only names, project saving, and WAV/MIDI exports. I only exercised this small workflow; the WAV dialog exposed limited format choices.

findings.observation: The visible Double-click for MIDI hint opened the device library; Assign instrument produced a MIDI track visibly assigned to Rill Lab Sine.
Pencil drags produced four labeled short notes in the piano roll, which also appeared as arrangement thumbnails.
Rename controls supplied an on-screen keyboard, enabling the pattern name pulse and project title neon pulse using mouse clicks. Save and export pickers then reused the project title.
Dragging a clip with Duplicate active produced no visible copy. The expected gesture was not obvious from the tool name alone.
Tool help explicitly said to click a clip; a click then made an adjacent copy, and box-selection allowed several MIDI clips to be duplicated together.
The first audio-edge trim left the arrangement at 30.134 seconds while the loop read 30.000. A small corrective drag did not visibly change it.
Switching snap from 1/16 to 1 bar and dragging the audio edge aligned the final audio and MIDI ends; the saved arrangement title read 0:30.000.
During playback the button read Pause, both track meters lit, and a subsequent screenshot showed the playhead at 006.01.92.
WAV export showed the arrangement duration and an effect-tail checkbox; turning tails off displayed 0:30. Completion notices were displayed for both neon pulse.wav and neon pulse.mid.
Some native dialogs appeared after the initial screenshot, and the first MIDI-export screenshot briefly showed a black dialog-sized area before the picker rendered.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: a named 30-second arrangement was saved and both exports showed success notices. Output contents and durations await independent verification.
outcome.composition: 112 BPM, 4/4. Fourteen one-bar MIDI clips repeating short C4, C4, G4, E4 notes through Rill Lab Sine, over three full copies and a final two-bar portion of the startup Circuit rhythm audio. Loop spans 1:1.00 to 15:1.00, visibly 0:00.000 to 0:30.000.
outcome.playback_observed: Play changed to Pause, both track meters lit, and the playhead advanced from the start to 006.01.92. Stop returned the transport to the beginning. No audio was auditioned.

limitations: No output file contents or heard audio were verified; independent coordinator verification follows.
Only the visible application was used for composition and output. No keyboard events, shortcuts, APIs, implementation inspection, or other participant records were used.
Software graphics and a virtual audio backend were laboratory conditions; timing impressions do not establish physical-device latency or audio quality.
Only the installed Rill Lab Sine instrument was used; this does not establish compatibility with other third-party plug-ins.
The arrangement is deliberately simple and repetitive; its musical balance and audible result were not evaluated by listening.
Session elapsed time includes tool, screenshot, and reporting overhead and is not a performance benchmark.
